title: Scalp rotation
brief: A 15 mm SCC on the scalp. With a 6 mm margin the defect is 27 mm across. Scalp skin is thick and barely stretches: close it with a rotation flap.
goals: Design a rotation flap with a long arc (about 4 times the defect's width) and undermine widely.
Rotate it in, tie the key sutures, close the rest; watch the sutures under the scalp's tension.

approach.text: A large rotation flap: a long arc (several times the defect's width) swung round a pivot, with wide undermining under the galea. A back-cut or Burow's triangle at the base helps it turn. Suggested here: the direction with the least closure tension in the simulator.

tips.lesion: The margin circle must lie inside the defect all round.
tips.closed: The scalp pulls hard: close the remaining gaps with several sutures.
tips.tension: Lengthen the arc (Length : width in the Flap panel) and undermine further (Undermine beyond).
tips.dog_ears: A dog-ear at the pivot is common: a Burow's triangle there removes it.
tips.sutures: Scalp closures need stronger thread (3-0 or 4-0) or less tension.
